highlights.content: Upstage Unveils "Solar Pro 4" as First Korean Model Listed on OpenRouter Language KR CN ### News #### News #### Special Economic Content Platform for Investors Language KR CN # Upstage Unveils "Solar Pro 4" as First Korean Model Listed on OpenRouter by *Lee Myeonghwan* Published 14 Aug.2026 09:29(KST) ## LLM Specialized for AI Agents, Dramatically Enhanced Agent Performance First Korean Model Listed on Developer Platform OpenRouter Outperforming NVIDIA and Google Models in Global Benchmarking Upstage announced on the 14th that it has released "Solar Pro 4," a large language model (LLM) specializing in artificial intelligence (AI) agents that was developed in-house. Solar Pro 4 is Upstage's next-generation commercial AI model, built to enhance both reasoning capabilities and agent performance compared to its predecessor, Solar Pro 3. Going beyond single-turn answers, it is optimized for real work environments, excelling at document understanding and information extraction, long-context reasoning, and sequential decision-making tasks. ![Upstage announced on the 14th that it has unveiled 'Solar Pro 4,' a large language model (LLM) specialized for AI agents developed in-house. Upstage](https://cphoto.asiae.co.kr/listimglink/1/2026081409110680817_1786666266.png) Upstage announced on the 14th that it has unveiled 'Solar Pro 4,' a large language model (LLM) specialized for AI agents developed in-house. Upstage Immediately after its release, Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to be listed on a global developer platform. It was the only Korean model included in the AI agent "Hermes Agent" developed by NUS Research in the U.S. and the API routing platform "OpenRouter." Upstage became the first Korean company to be registered as an official provider among major U.S. big tech firms like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and NVIDIA, as well as leading Chinese companies such as DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax. As Solar Pro 4 was added to global platforms, real usage cases have also been increasing rapidly. Just three days after being listed on OpenRouter, Solar Pro 4 surpassed a cumulative token usage of 80 billion tokens, demonstrating growing interest from developers worldwide. Furthermore, Solar Pro 4 is the first Korean model to be included in the "Agent Arena" leaderboard, which compares the agent performance of prominent global models. The model proved to be on par with NVIDIA's "Nemotron 3 Ultra." While most models on this leaderboard are from the U.S. and China, Upstage is the first Korean company to have its model featured. Solar Pro 4 also achieved a score of 57 on "Terminal-Bench v2.1," which evaluates the ability to complete multi-step tasks in a terminal environment. This is 4.8 times higher than the previous version's score. In "Tau³-Banking (τ³-Banking)," which assesses conversational tool usage, it achieved a score of 23, representing a 2.6-fold improvement. The ability to handle long and complex documents is another major advantage. In the long-context reading benchmark (AA-LCR), which evaluates the extraction of information from substantial, lengthy documents and reasoning based on that information, Solar Pro 4 received a score of 71, 2.3 times higher than its predecessor. Korean language performance and document processing capabilities have also been enhanced. Solar Pro 4 is now incorporated into Upstage's integrated agent document processing solution, "Upstage Studio," enabling it to extract information from a variety of formats, including HWP documents, and perform summarization, analysis, translation, and other tasks. For overall capability, Solar Pro 4 scored 42 according to Artificial Analysis, a global AI evaluation institute, showing an improvement of more than three times compared to the previous version. Solar Pro 4 even outperformed major big tech models, such as NVIDIA's "Nemotron 3 Ultra" (38 points) and Google's "Gemini 3.5 Flash-Light" (37 points). ### Hot Picks Today [![[Exclusive] Hyundai Motor Retirees Fa...

highlights.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) ![](https://img.youtube.com/vi/HC8T1OlgYi0/hqdefault.jpg) [Stop being skeptical about AI for development with Charity Majors](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HC8T1OlgYi0) HostGergely OroszGuestCharity Majors yesterday01:26:24en ![](/images/img_default_profile@2x.png)[The Pragmatic Engineer](/podcast?source=The%20Pragmatic%20Engineer) ## Key Takeaways Honeycomb CTO Charity Majors argues that shipping unread AI code is acceptable when backed by robust telemetry and conformance testing, and that observability, not code review, is the key to maintaining reliability in AI-driven development. ## Summary Charity Majors has spent the past year and a half doing what her own skeptics would respect: changing her mind in public. The Honeycomb co-founder and CEO — previously an engineer at Linden Lab on Second Life, then at Parse through its Facebook acquisition, where she watched the internal tool Scuba transform debugging — opened 2025 treating AI as a big feature, "bigger than a programming language, like the cloud, but not generational." By November 2025, when Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 4.5, she had revised that judgment. Recorded in person with Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer) in early August 2026, this episode is Majors' full account of why the honest question is no longer *whether* engineers will ship code they have not read — but *when*, and what must be true for that to become acceptable. The episode's load-bearing argument is a trust ledger. AI debits trust at the point of creation — code appears that no human has reviewed or understood — so the industry must rebuild that trust somewhere else: tests, evals, conformance testing, harnesses, and production telemetry. The disciplines that make this possible, she argues, already exist in the two domains software engineers have historically been snobbish about: ops and QA. In parallel, she makes the case that both warring factions in the AI wars are empirically correct — the enthusiasts are winning in measurable ways, and the people on call are watching systems get worse — and that reliability across the industry is quietly degrading, with Meta's SEV-0 flurry and Intercom's 18-month slump as public evidence. The conversation also covers her unboxing of code review, the DevOps movement's partial failure, a new observability primitive for AI agents, and a specific career playbook for managers, directors, and junior engineers. ## Both AI camps are right, and talking past each other Majors traces her own conversion arc precisely. In March 2025 she and Fred Hébert gave the closing keynote at SREcon, pitching "vibe coding" to **audible groans** from the audience; the term had just been invented. Her pitch then was deliberately modest — learn AI "because you can complain better if you learn it," which she insists she meant literally. The turning point was November 2025's Opus 4.5 — but she is careful to note that the models were not the whole story: "in retrospect you could see it coming sooner... it wasn't actually the models, it was the harnesses, it was all the tooling." By July 2025, the people already using Claude Code, P.I., and OpenCode were saying "this is coming faster than you think." By early 2026, "everyone around me was just trying it again and changing their mind." She defends the earlier skepticism rather than apologizing for it: the claim that AI would write code about as well as the median engineer had been made repeatedly before, under different names — neural nets, COBOL, no-code/low-code — and had been wrong each time. Her formulation is "we were right and we were wrong": right to disbelieve the first generation of claims, wrong to assume the latest one would fail too. highlights.content: # vals.ai raises $40M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz ![vals.ai raises $40M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz](https://sg-imgs.dealroom.co/99064754377d90735e4c548f1a4332d9.jpeg) **What's the deal?** [vals.ai](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/vals_ai) has raised $40 million in a Series A round led by [Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)](https://app.dealroom.co/investors/andreessen_horowitz) to build independent evaluation benchmarks for AI models. The company tests frontier large language models (LLMs) on tasks businesses actually pay for — financial analysis, coding, legal research, and web search — rather than abstract logic puzzles. **Why now?** Most widely cited benchmarks were built for academic contexts, and model developers increasingly optimise for them directly. That leaves enterprise buyers unable to compare models when [OpenAI](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/openai_1), [Anthropic](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/anthropic), [Google](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/google_gooru), and [Meta](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/meta_5) all claim top scores on overlapping tests. **What's the endgame?** vals.ai's flagship product, the Vals Index, aggregates performance across real-world categories and ranks models. Its August 2026 update placed Claude Fable 5 on top with a score of 75.14%. The company runs several specialised benchmarks, including the Finance Agent Benchmark and the Web Search Index, built with domain experts rather than machine learning researchers alone. **The new products:** Alongside the funding, vals.ai announced new products, signalling a push beyond benchmarking as a standalone offering and into continuous model monitoring. The $40 million should fund expansion into new verticals, hiring domain experts, and tooling that lets enterprise customers run evaluations on their own proprietary data. The round is a sharp step up for a company described as bootstrapped with an estimated $1.3 million in annual recurring revenue as recently as late 2025. **The signal:** Andreessen Horowitz has backed AI companies across the stack, from chip design to application layers. Adding vals.ai suggests it sees the evaluation layer as underfunded relative to its importance — as buyers increasingly need trustworthy numbers to choose between competing models. *Image credit: Generated with Gemini* Read more: [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/vals-ai-40m-series-a-a16z/) 77 ### Read more ### Dealroom Ask AI Beta Get AI-powered insights ### Start a conversation Ask anything about this entity Suggested questions: All answers are AI generated. highlights.content: ![]() ![MarketBeat](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/marketbeat--theme-light.svg) ![MarketBeat](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/marketbeat--theme-dark.svg) # Docebo Sees Growth Accelerate as Enterprise, AI and Skills Bets Gain Traction ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/docebo.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/docebo.svg) ![Docebo logo](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/marketbeat:72839fb78094b-ae3dd01a2059c667f4c682ed8f0c7fe7-resized.webp) Docebo [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/docebo.svg)DCBO](/symbols/NASDAQ-DCBO/) said its underlying growth accelerated for a second consecutive quarter as the company gains traction with larger enterprise customers, expands its artificial intelligence product portfolio and begins integrating its recent skills-intelligence acquisition. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/docebo.svg) Speaking at Canaccord’s 46th Annual Growth Conference in Boston, Chief Executive Officer Alessio Artuffo said the learning-platform provider has spent the past several years increasing its enterprise focus. That work has begun to show results through accelerating pipeline activity, larger customer contracts and new product releases, he said. “We’re signing bigger customers at bigger tickets,” Artuffo said, adding that the company is progressing toward becoming a more strategic enterprise-focused platform after beginning its public-company history with greater exposure to mid-market and small-business customers. ARR Growth Expected to Reaccelerate Chief Financial Officer Brandon Farber said reported annual recurring revenue grew 9.5% in the second quarter. The company’s core ARR, which excludes foreign exchange effects, acquired ARR and the wind-down of its Dayforce business, rose 13.9%. Farber said Docebo expects reported ARR growth to begin converging with core ARR growth during the second half as the company laps prior churn from Dayforce and Amazon Web Services. Dayforce represented about $19.5 million in ARR roughly a year earlier and about $16.5 million at the time of the conference, according to Farber. He said the company faced approximately $5 million of Dayforce churn in the third quarter of the prior year, followed by approximately $4 million of AWS churn in the fourth quarter, in addition to Dayforce churn. Management cited enterprise momentum, steady mid-market performance and improving international business as drivers of the acceleration. Farber also said Docebo is seeing enterprise sales cycles compress, though he noted that several factors can affect deal timing. He identified go-to-market execution as the largest controllable contributor, alongside improved product positioning and the addition of skills capabilities. Skills Acquisition Broadens Enterprise Opportunity Earlier this year, Docebo acquired French skills-intelligence platform 365Talents and AI-native enterprise-search company Zive. Artuffo said the company began seeing results from the 365Talents integration in the second quarter, with some large customers adopting the combined skills-and-learning offering. Farber said the skills component has helped raise contract value and has opened opportunities that Docebo may not have won previously as a standalone learning-management-system vendor. In two recently discussed deals involving a large telecommunications company and an automotive company, skills capabilities were a key requirement, he said. The company also expects its FedRAMP business to contribute to the second half. Farber said the company typically excludes individual deals with more than $1 million in ARR from its guidance, while noting that FedRAMP opportunities are often large and can be uneven in timing. Docebo’s second quarter was its strongest quarter for state, local and education, or SLED, business, he said, adding that FedRAMP certification has also improved the company’s credibility in that market. The Honeycomb co-founder and CEO — previously an engineer at Linden Lab on Second Life, then at Parse through its Facebook acquisition, where she watched the internal tool Scuba transform debugging — opened 2025 treating AI as a big feature, "bigger than a programming language, like the cloud, but not generational." By November 2025, when Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 4.5, she had revised that judgment. Recorded in person with Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer) in early August 2026, this episode is Majors' full account of why the honest question is no longer *whether* engineers will ship code they have not read — but *when*, and what must be true for that to become acceptable. The episode's load-bearing argument is a trust ledger. AI debits trust at the point of creation — code appears that no human has reviewed or understood — so the industry must rebuild that trust somewhere else: tests, evals, conformance testing, harnesses, and production telemetry. The disciplines that make this possible, she argues, already exist in the two domains software engineers have historically been snobbish about: ops and QA. In parallel, she makes the case that both warring factions in the AI wars are empirically correct — the enthusiasts are winning in measurable ways, and the people on call are watching systems get worse — and that reliability across the industry is quietly degrading, with Meta's SEV-0 flurry and Intercom's 18-month slump as public evidence. The conversation also covers her unboxing of code review, the DevOps movement's partial failure, a new observability primitive for AI agents, and a specific career playbook for managers, directors, and junior engineers. ## Both AI camps are right, and talking past each other Majors traces her own conversion arc precisely. In March 2025 she and Fred Hébert gave the closing keynote at SREcon, pitching "vibe coding" to **audible groans** from the audience; the term had just been invented. Her pitch then was deliberately modest — learn AI "because you can complain better if you learn it," which she insists she meant literally. The turning point was November 2025's Opus 4.5 — but she is careful to note that the models were not the whole story: "in retrospect you could see it coming sooner... it wasn't actually the models, it was the harnesses, it was all the tooling." By July 2025, the people already using Claude Code, P.I., and OpenCode were saying "this is coming faster than you think." By early 2026, "everyone around me was just trying it again and changing their mind." She defends the earlier skepticism rather than apologizing for it: the claim that AI would write code about as well as the median engineer had been made repeatedly before, under different names — neural nets, COBOL, no-code/low-code — and had been wrong each time. Her formulation is "we were right and we were wrong": right to disbelieve the first generation of claims, wrong to assume the latest one would fail too. BOLD is a U.K.-based AI research lab led by the University of Oxford that brings together researchers affiliated with the University of Oxford, University College London and Imperial College London. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AMD-shutterstock_2792614943-300x200.jpg) Credit: Erman Gunes/Shutterstock The MOU focuses on BOLD’s research into paradigm-breaking discoveries in fundamental AI. Together, AMD and BOLD researchers intend to explore initiatives spanning compute access, software optimization, research collaboration and open-source development. BOLD researchers anticipate experiments to explore model training techniques beyond backpropagation, discovery using multi-agent systems and adaptive physical AI. “BOLD aims to advance a more open, efficient and human-centered path for AI through collaboration between academia and industry,” said Associate Professor Jakob Foerster, Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford. “Working with AMD, the University of Oxford would combine world-leading research with computing technology to test ideas, learn quickly and translate breakthroughs into applications. This support would help BOLD develop approaches to learning, human-AI collaboration and embodied intelligence while expanding open access to computing resources that benefit science, healthcare, education, transportation and public services globally.” “Through our memorandum of understanding with the BOLD lab, AMD is exploring bringing together advanced computing, open software and technical expertise to help researchers pursue ambitious new frontiers in AI,” said Thomas Zacharia, senior vice president, Global Public Sector and Strategic Partnerships at AMD. “By expanding access to compute and supporting open academic research, our aim would be to help BOLD researchers accelerate experimentation and contribute to the U.K.’s leadership in AI innovation and scientific discovery.” As part of the MOU, AMD would provide up to 5 million pounds in compute resources for BOLD researchers. LLMs.content: Upstage Unveils "Solar Pro 4" as First Korean Model Listed on OpenRouter Language KR CN ### News #### News #### Special Economic Content Platform for Investors Language KR CN # Upstage Unveils "Solar Pro 4" as First Korean Model Listed on OpenRouter by *Lee Myeonghwan* Published 14 Aug.2026 09:29(KST) ## LLM Specialized for AI Agents, Dramatically Enhanced Agent Performance First Korean Model Listed on Developer Platform OpenRouter Outperforming NVIDIA and Google Models in Global Benchmarking Upstage announced on the 14th that it has released "Solar Pro 4," a large language model (LLM) specializing in artificial intelligence (AI) agents that was developed in-house. Solar Pro 4 is Upstage's next-generation commercial AI model, built to enhance both reasoning capabilities and agent performance compared to its predecessor, Solar Pro 3. Going beyond single-turn answers, it is optimized for real work environments, excelling at document understanding and information extraction, long-context reasoning, and sequential decision-making tasks. ![Upstage announced on the 14th that it has unveiled 'Solar Pro 4,' a large language model (LLM) specialized for AI agents developed in-house. Upstage](https://cphoto.asiae.co.kr/listimglink/1/2026081409110680817_1786666266.png) Upstage announced on the 14th that it has unveiled 'Solar Pro 4,' a large language model (LLM) specialized for AI agents developed in-house. Upstage Immediately after its release, Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to be listed on a global developer platform. It was the only Korean model included in the AI agent "Hermes Agent" developed by NUS Research in the U.S. and the API routing platform "OpenRouter." Upstage became the first Korean company to be registered as an official provider among major U.S. big tech firms like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and NVIDIA, as well as leading Chinese companies such as DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax. As Solar Pro 4 was added to global platforms, real usage cases have also been increasing rapidly. Just three days after being listed on OpenRouter, Solar Pro 4 surpassed a cumulative token usage of 80 billion tokens, demonstrating growing interest from developers worldwide. Furthermore, Solar Pro 4 is the first Korean model to be included in the "Agent Arena" leaderboard, which compares the agent performance of prominent global models. The model proved to be on par with NVIDIA's "Nemotron 3 Ultra." While most models on this leaderboard are from the U.S. and China, Upstage is the first Korean company to have its model featured. Solar Pro 4 also achieved a score of 57 on "Terminal-Bench v2.1," which evaluates the ability to complete multi-step tasks in a terminal environment. This is 4.8 times higher than the previous version's score. In "Tau³-Banking (τ³-Banking)," which assesses conversational tool usage, it achieved a score of 23, representing a 2.6-fold improvement. The ability to handle long and complex documents is another major advantage. In the long-context reading benchmark (AA-LCR), which evaluates the extraction of information from substantial, lengthy documents and reasoning based on that information, Solar Pro 4 received a score of 71, 2.3 times higher than its predecessor. Korean language performance and document processing capabilities have also been enhanced. Solar Pro 4 is now incorporated into Upstage's integrated agent document processing solution, "Upstage Studio," enabling it to extract information from a variety of formats, including HWP documents, and perform summarization, analysis, translation, and other tasks. For overall capability, Solar Pro 4 scored 42 according to Artificial Analysis, a global AI evaluation institute, showing an improvement of more than three times compared to the previous version. LLMs.content: # vals.ai raises $40M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz ![vals.ai raises $40M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz](https://sg-imgs.dealroom.co/99064754377d90735e4c548f1a4332d9.jpeg) **What's the deal?** [vals.ai](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/vals_ai) has raised $40 million in a Series A round led by [Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)](https://app.dealroom.co/investors/andreessen_horowitz) to build independent evaluation benchmarks for AI models. The company tests frontier large language models (LLMs) on tasks businesses actually pay for — financial analysis, coding, legal research, and web search — rather than abstract logic puzzles. **Why now?** Most widely cited benchmarks were built for academic contexts, and model developers increasingly optimise for them directly. That leaves enterprise buyers unable to compare models when [OpenAI](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/openai_1), [Anthropic](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/anthropic), [Google](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/google_gooru), and [Meta](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/meta_5) all claim top scores on overlapping tests. **What's the endgame?** vals.ai's flagship product, the Vals Index, aggregates performance across real-world categories and ranks models. Its August 2026 update placed Claude Fable 5 on top with a score of 75.14%. The company runs several specialised benchmarks, including the Finance Agent Benchmark and the Web Search Index, built with domain experts rather than machine learning researchers alone. **The new products:** Alongside the funding, vals.ai announced new products, signalling a push beyond benchmarking as a standalone offering and into continuous model monitoring. The $40 million should fund expansion into new verticals, hiring domain experts, and tooling that lets enterprise customers run evaluations on their own proprietary data. The round is a sharp step up for a company described as bootstrapped with an estimated $1.3 million in annual recurring revenue as recently as late 2025. **The signal:** Andreessen Horowitz has backed AI companies across the stack, from chip design to application layers. The company published an expert roundtable featuring the researchers and engineers behind the model, sharing what makes this new release stand out in an increasingly crowded field of [large language models](https://blog.google/technology/ai/). While technical specifications remain sparse, the move signals Google's continued push to differentiate its Gemini family from competitors like [OpenAI](https://openai.com) and [Anthropic](https://anthropic.com). [Google](https://google.com) is making its move in the AI model wars with Gemini Omni, a new addition to its Gemini family that the company's experts are calling a significant step forward. The announcement, published on [Google's official blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-omni-experts-roundtable/), takes an unusual approach - instead of a traditional product launch, the company assembled a roundtable of [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google) experts to discuss what excites them most about the model. The "Omni" naming convention is telling. It echoes the industry's recent obsession with omnimodal AI systems that can process text, images, audio, and video simultaneously. [OpenAI](https://openai.com) sparked this trend with GPT-4o earlier this year, and now Google appears ready to stake its claim in the same territory. Contributor Lindsey Lanquist conducted the interviews, though the full technical specifications and benchmark results remain under wraps for now. What we're seeing is Google trying a different playbook. Rather than dropping a massive technical paper or holding a splashy product demo, the company's letting its researchers do the talking. It's a calculated move that positions Gemini Omni as a product of deep expertise rather than pure marketing hype. The strategy could resonate with enterprise customers who've grown skeptical of AI companies overselling capabilities. The timing isn't accidental. [Microsoft](https://microsoft.com) has been aggressively integrating AI across its product suite, while [Meta](https://meta.com) continues pushing Llama models into the open-source community. Google needs to prove that Gemini isn't just another ChatGPT competitor but a fundamentally different approach to AI. The expert roundtable format suggests confidence in the underlying technology - when you let engineers explain their work without a script, you're betting they'll say something compelling. The company rushed out Bard, rebranded to Gemini, and has been iterating rapidly ever since. LLMs.title: Upstage unveils Solar Pro 4, first Korean AI model listed on OpenRouter - The Herald Business
LLMs.titleZh: Upstage unveils Solar Pro 4, first Korean AI model listed on OpenRouter - The Herald Business
LLMs.content: ![](https://static.heraldcorp.com/wbazic/biz/mobile/image/header_gnb_country_1.png) # Upstage unveils Solar Pro 4, first Korean AI model listed on OpenRouter View Korean Original First Korean model on global developer platform Agent performance sharply improved for real-world tasks AAII score of 42 outpaces Big Tech rivals ![A promotional image for Upstage's AI model Solar Pro 4 [Upstage]](https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/08/14/news-p.v1.20260814.41f20f195cda407aace11b96e2a37ad6_P1.png) Upstage has unveiled Solar Pro 4, a large language model with enhanced reasoning and AI agent capabilities, becoming the first Korean AI model listed on OpenRouter, a global developer platform. The company said Friday it released Solar Pro 4, its next-generation commercial AI model. The new model improves on its predecessor, Solar Pro 3, in reasoning and agent performance, and is designed to reliably handle the complex workflows demanded in real-world work environments. According to Upstage, Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to appear on a global developer platform immediately after its launch. It was listed on Hermes Agent, an AI agent developed by US-based Nous Research, and on OpenRouter, an API routing platform. Upstage said it is the first Korean company registered as an official provider on OpenRouter alongside major US technology companies and leading Chinese firms. Developer uptake was swift. Solar Pro 4 surpassed 80 billion tokens in cumulative consumption within three days of its OpenRouter listing. Upstage also said Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to enter the Agent Arena leaderboard, which compares agent performance across major global models. The model ranked on par with Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra. Upstage said it focused on improving "agentic tasks" in developing this model. Solar Pro 4 scored 57 on TerminalBench, a benchmark that evaluates a model's ability to complete multi-step tasks in a terminal from start to finish — 4.8 times higher than its predecessor. It also scored 23 on Tau3-Banking, a benchmark assessing tool-use ability through multi-turn dialogue, a 2.6-fold improvement. Another key feature of Solar Pro 4 is its ability to handle long and complex documents. The model scored 71 on AA-LCR, a long-context comprehension benchmark that evaluates a model's ability to extract information from lengthy documents and reason toward an answer — more than 2.3 times better than its predecessor. Upstage said the model's reduced tendency to lose context in the middle of documents improved not only accuracy but also token efficiency. Korean-language performance tailored to the office environments of domestic companies and public institutions has also improved. Solar Pro 4 is set to be integrated into Upstage Studio, the company's all-in-one agent document processing solution. The model can extract information from a wide range of document formats, including hangul documents, and handle tasks such as summarization, analysis and translation. Solar Pro 4 scored 42 overall on the Artificial Analysis AI benchmark, more than three times the score of its predecessor. It outperformed Big Tech models including Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra, which scored 38, and Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite at 37. It also posted a wide margin over competing sovereign models such as Mistral's Medium 3.5, which scored 30, and Cohere's Command A+ at 23. "What AI needs in the real world is not the ability to ace tests, but the reliability to see a job through to the end," said Kim Sung-hoon, CEO of Upstage. "Solar Pro 4 becoming the first Korean model listed on a global developer platform is proof that our AI technology works on the world stage, and we will continue building AI that is even more practical and useful." LLMs.content: * [Home](/) * [Tech](/personaltech) * [Artificial Intelligence](/artificial-intelligence) # Motif 3 Final Release: MIT License Opens Korea’s Sovereign AI to Builders #### No announcement, full MIT license: ~30-person team’s final 314B MoE now buildable By [Devin Culbertson](https://www.techtimes.com/reporters/devin-culbertson) [Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324260/20260813/motif-3-final-release-mit-license-opens-koreas-sovereign-ai-builders.htm) [Share on Twitter](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Motif+3+Final+Release%3A+MIT+License+Opens+Korea%27s+Sovereign+AI+to+Builders+https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324260/20260813/motif-3-final-release-mit-license-opens-koreas-sovereign-ai-builders.htm) [Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.techtimes.com%2Farticles%2F324260%2F20260813%2Fmotif-3-final-release-mit-license-opens-koreas-sovereign-ai-builders.htm&title=Motif+3+Final+Release%3A+MIT+License+Opens+Korea%27s+Sovereign+AI+to+Builders) [Share on Reddit](http://reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324260/20260813/motif-3-final-release-mit-license-opens-koreas-sovereign-ai-builders.htm&title=Motif+3+Final+Release%3A+MIT+License+Opens+Korea%27s+Sovereign+AI+to+Builders) [Share on Flipboard](https://flipboard.com) [Share on Pocket](https://getpocket.com/edit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324260/20260813/motif-3-final-release-mit-license-opens-koreas-sovereign-ai-builders.htm) Motiftech.io Motif Technologies shipped the final weights of its Motif 3 language model to Hugging Face this week without a press release, a blog post, or anything on motiftech.io — just three repositories that appeared within minutes of each other and a [Motif 3 arXiv technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09119) published simultaneously. The commercially meaningful part is not the model's parameter count. It is the license: Motif-3-Base, the instruction-tuned Motif-3, and the quantized Motif-3-NVFP4 are all released under the [MIT License on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Motif-Technologies/Motif-3), the most permissive standard available — a direct upgrade from the non-commercial research restriction that had blocked commercial use of July's Motif-3-Beta since its release. The practical difference is significant: any fine-tuning provider, enterprise, or startup that was waiting for the licensing call to Seoul can now proceed without one. ### What Motif 3 Is — and What Makes Its Architecture Worth Examining Motif 3 is a Mixture-of-Experts language model with 314 billion total parameters and 13.2 billion activated per token — specifications [from the official model card](https://huggingface.co/Motif-Technologies/Motif-3). The sparse-activation design — routing 8 of 384 experts plus one shared expert per token — means that inference costs are comparable to a dense model of roughly 13 billion parameters, while the model's total knowledge capacity draws on the full 314-billion-parameter pool. The model was pretrained on approximately [12.5 trillion tokens across domains](https://huggingface.co/Motif-Technologies/Motif-3), covering web documents, STEM, code, mathematics, and Korean-language data, and it supports a native 262,144-token context window (256K tokens). What distinguishes Motif 3 architecturally are two proprietary components Motif describes as wholly in-house designs — not re-parameterizations of any existing open-source architecture. The first is **Grouped Differential Latent Attention (GDLA)**. KORA rated 6,134 of 14,839 simulated conversations as failing, equivalent to 41%. No product received its highest A grade, while the average grade for apps operating in child mode was C. The overall scores combine two evaluations. An AI agent role-playing a child held conversations with each app before another large language model judged the responses. KORA also audited product features including app listings, privacy policies, onboarding, account settings and live interfaces. Scenarios covered users aged 7-9, 10-12 and 13-17, and tested 26 child safety risks. Seven products were examined in both child and adult modes, two only in child mode and three only through their adult experience. KORA reported overall scores of 59 for ChatGPT in child mode and 54 in adult mode. Copilot scored 53 and 46 respectively, while Gemini received 45 in child mode and 40 in adult mode. KORA’s statistical tests found no significant overall difference for any of the seven matched products, with all p-values above .14. The benchmark did find small but statistically significant improvements in conversational safety for the child versions of ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini. None received an overall grade above C. #### **Education apps lead the table but retain safety gaps** MagicSchool achieved the highest overall score, receiving 74 out of 100 and a B grade. It was the only app to reach that grade. ChatGPT’s child mode followed with 59, while SchoolAI scored 57. Both received C grades. Khanmigo recorded 56 in child mode and 55 in adult mode, also placing both versions in the C band. KORA defines a C score of 40-59 as meeting a minimum standard while retaining notable gaps. PolyBuzz and Character.AI occupied the bottom of the table, each scoring 27 and receiving D grades. Across the benchmark, child-mode experiences produced a failing response in approximately one-third of conversations. Adult experiences failed around half. KORA said the three highest-ranked variants, MagicSchool, ChatGPT child mode and SchoolAI, collectively failed 20% of conversations. The results also identified a weakness connected directly to schoolwork. KORA reported failure rates of between 62% and 88% for ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and Meta AI in conversations testing educational and epistemic integrity. AI Product.content: [![https://cdn.pseo.one/66f5089e70f7451d19ff67d9/assets/images/logo/7647630a-c618-4660-9d48-b6937466ecff.svg](https://cdn.pseo.one/66f5089e70f7451d19ff67d9/assets/images/logo/7647630a-c618-4660-9d48-b6937466ecff.svg)](https://gracker.ai/blog "GrackerAI") [Sign In](https://portal.gracker.ai/) [Sign Up](https://portal.gracker.ai) # Why AI Search Visibility Should Be Part of Every AI Product Launch Strategy AI search visibility AI product launch strategy generative search visibility AI product discoverability AI search monitoring ![Govind Kumar](https://cdn.pseo.one/66f5089e70f7451d19ff67d9/topical/authors-image/94c60990-6957-4a19-b287-33c860f35b69.jpg) Govind Kumar Co-founder/CPO August 13, 2026 6 min read ![Why AI Search Visibility Should Be Part of Every AI Product Launch Strategy](https://cdn.pseo.one/66f5089e70f7451d19ff67d9/687e1c1ef6fe799d288518df/6a7d9eb92907e487223f9193/why-ai-search-visibility-should-be-part-of-every-ai-product-launch-strategy/feature-image.jpg) Launching an AI product used to follow a relatively straightforward sequence. Teams focused on model accuracy, engineering stability, infrastructure costs, user acquisition campaigns, and product messaging. Marketing departments concentrated on website traffic, backlinks, keyword rankings, and social engagement, while product managers monitored activation rates, retention, and customer feedback. The rise of generative search systems has altered this process considerably. Today, potential customers increasingly rely on conversational interfaces to identify software vendors, compare solutions, understand market categories, and evaluate competing products. Decision-makers who once opened ten browser tabs now ask AI assistants to summarize available options, explain differences between providers, and recommend solutions for specific business problems. This shift introduces an entirely new visibility challenge. A company may launch a technically sophisticated AI product, secure media mentions, publish extensive documentation, and maintain strong search rankings, yet still remain largely absent from AI-generated responses. If conversational systems cannot confidently explain what the product does, identify its use cases, or associate it with a particular category, discoverability becomes limited despite significant investment in development and marketing. The question is no longer whether organizations should think about AI visibility. The question is when visibility planning should begin. Increasingly, the answer appears to be long before launch day. ## Why AI Visibility Has Become A Product Distribution Channel ### Search Behavior Is Changing Faster Than Launch Strategies Product launches often rely on frameworks developed during an era dominated by traditional search engines. Teams optimize landing pages, coordinate public relations campaigns, prepare webinars, and publish educational content designed to capture traffic through conventional keyword searches. User behavior, however, is evolving rapidly. Someone researching cybersecurity software may ask an assistant which vendors specialize in threat intelligence. A marketing leader exploring AI content solutions might request recommendations for platforms that monitor brand mentions inside generative search environments. Procurement teams evaluating development partners increasingly expect conversational systems to provide vendor comparisons before they visit company websites. These interactions are fundamentally different from traditional searches because users are seeking synthesized recommendations rather than lists of documents. Companies that ignore this change risk optimizing for visibility channels that account for a shrinking proportion of discovery journeys. ### AI-Generated Answers Influence Product Discovery Generative systems act as information intermediaries. Open Source AI.content: [Home](/en) Article # Just now, DeepSeek Harness has been stunningly open-sourced: Everything is a plugin. 机器之心2026-08-14 07:41 We have already conducted the internal beta test in advance. Earlier this morning, the official version of DeepSeek V4 Pro was released, setting off a wave of excitement. Now, just half a day later, **DeepSeek Harness** (Developer Preview) is here! This hardly comes as a surprise, as the project has been in the works for a long time. For instance, Cui Tianyi from the DeepSeek Harness team has been posting previews on social platforms and recruiting talent for the team. We also obtained the internal test access to DeepSeek Harness in early August, getting an early experience of this agent framework that is destined to bring new transformations to the AI community. Open source repository: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness For example, we used DeepSeek Harness configured with the official DeepSeek-V4-Flash to build a first-person zombie shooting game. Without any manual intervention midway, we got a fairly playable finished product in just over 30 minutes, even if it is not perfectly polished. Considering that Andrej Karpathy's recent idea of generating 3D worlds with AI has gone viral, we also challenged DeepSeek Harness (V4-Flash) with the classic benchmark "Huang Qiang Buying Watermelon": to recreate the classic "Huang Qiang Buying Watermelon" clip into a 3D animation based on text description (this is also the result of one-shot prompting): Overall, although it is still far from perfect, the general plot of this animation is largely restored, and the character relationships are also clearly recognizable. In comparison, the animation we produced using the exact same prompt with Codex configured with GPT-5.6 sol-xhigh is far less satisfactory: It should be noted that the parameter scale of DeepSeek-V4-Flash is much smaller than that of GPT-5.6 sol. It is easy to imagine that DeepSeek Harness has played a huge role in delivering such performance. Today, with the release of the official version of DeepSeek V4 Pro, we have also connected this model to DeepSeek Harness and run the test again: The performance is indeed noticeably better. Next, let's take a look at the project structure, which is quite impressive: **the repository already contains more than 230 workspace members**, with code distributed in directories including packages/, apps/, examples/, python/, native/, vendor/, website/ and more. File system, terminal, subprocess, PTY, language server, web access, skills, sub-agents, workflows, planning mode, session persistence, settings, credentials, telemetry - almost every single capability has its own dedicated package. If we compare an ordinary Agent project to a fully assembled pre-built computer, DeepSeek Harness is more like a massive breadboard: models, tools, interfaces, storage, security policies and context management can all be plugged in, and they can also be unplugged whenever needed. It provides a default assembly solution, but it is clear that what DeepSeek really wants to create is not a fixed-form "DeepSeek coding assistant", but **a universal way to assemble agents**. ## **What is DeepSeek Harness?** Let's first clarify a common point of confusion: DeepSeek Harness is not a new DeepSeek model, nor a simple API client. It is **a complete set of SDK and application framework for building, running and extending agents**. By default, it can connect to DeepSeek models (and can also be easily customized to connect to other models), allowing the model to read projects, modify files, run commands, manage tasks, assign subtasks, and interact with users through Web UI, full-screen terminal, Headless commands or automation protocols. The web version of DeepSeek Harness provides a convenient entry for directly configuring other model services, so users do not need to manually edit configuration files. In blind developer testing it beat every rival on a leaderboard for frontend coding ([The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/kimis-open-model-k3-nears-gpt-5-6-sol-and-fable-5-while-signaling-the-end-of-super-cheap-chinese-ai/), July 16; [Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/moonshot-releases-2-8-trillion-parameter-kimi-k3), July 17). Dean Ball, a former senior policy advisor for AI and emerging technology in the White House who now heads strategic futures at OpenAI, wrote on social media that he was surprised Beijing still allows a model this capable to release with open weights ([X/@deanwball](https://archive.ph/4MXXC), July 17). On July 27, Moonshot uploaded the full weights one day ahead of schedule ([Hugging Face](https://archive.ph/YYEL3), accessed July 30). A communist party-state that prioritizes control yet tolerates and encourages open weight models may look strange. Beijing’s bet on open weights, however, is part of a national strategy in which supporting open weights acts as a hedge against U.S. computing export bans, widens its domestic AI chip manufacturing ecosystem, and brings PRC technical standards to Global South countries. Beijing has not ignored the security risks that open weight models may have, and may introduce a “tiered governance” (分级管理) framework to balance these risks going forward. **A Gift to the Global South** At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (世界人工智能大会) in Shanghai in July, 29 countries signed on as founding members of a new World AI Cooperation Organization (世界人工智能合作组织). Headquartered in Shanghai, this new institution aims to close the “intelligence gap” (智能鸿沟) for developing countries, through a set of promises detailed in Xi’s speech to the conference and an eight-point Action Plan from the National Development and Reform Commission ([Belt and Road Portal](https://archive.ph/yvllZ); [Xinhua](https://archive.ph/PNnFN); [NDRC](https://archive.ph/dr6oi), July 17; China Brief, [August 2, 2025](https://archive.ph/vNG32), [July 22](https://archive.ph/dsZJx), [August 12](https://archive.ph/smYXB)). The approach resembles one Beijing took more than a decade ago when it established the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). As in 2014, Beijing is creating a multilateral institution that will provide resources to support the development of Global South countries before Washington or other geopolitical actors propose an alternative. With the AIIB, the key resource was development finance; with WAICO, the main provision is model access. Unlike the complex processes involved in releasing financing to fund projects, however, this time, the benefits have already been handed over. Open Source AI.content: [About](/about-us) [Donate](/donate) Perspective # US Government’s AI Risk Review Should Apply to Open Weight Models Mark MacCarthy / Aug 13, 2026 ![ ](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/3tzzh18d/production/05bf71fb1a7f89634175a448753d5e282a57d2b9-1200x675.png) People visit the booth of Kimi, an LLM developed by the Chinese startup Moonshot, during the World AI Conference in Shanghai, China, Monday, July 20, 2026. (FeatureChina via AP Images) [Republish](/republish) Little is known about the Trump administration’s [secretive new](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/04/white-house-ai-vetting-plan-to-exempt-nonproprietary-models-01024816) voluntary safety review program for AI models. Yet one salient detail that is in the public domain is that it apparently [excludes](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/04/trump-ai-framework-open-models) open weight models. This exclusion would seem to include the highly-capable Chinese open models that are [widely used](https://openrouter.ai/rankings#leaderboard-table) by US startups and enterprises, but also the American open models such as those offered by [Meta](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/meta-muse-glimmer-open-weight-ai.html) and start-ups like [Reflection AI](https://reflection.ai/news). These models, apparently, will be allowed on the US market without any independent prior review. This exclusion seems to have stemmed in part from a successful campaign led by [Nvidia](https://images.nvidia.com/pdf/Open-Weights-and-American-AI-Leadership.pdf) and the newly-formed [Little Tech Association](https://static.politico.com/4a/bf/9c4021d8404386b0a311dcccf0e5/lta-open-weight-ai-letter-7-22-26.pdf) defending the value of open AI models. Developers of open weight models have chosen to publicly release the sequence of numerical values that control the output of the model, enabling users to download the model, modify it and use it on their own or rented compute infrastructure. Open weight models [promote competition](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-open-weight-models-are-crucial-for-american-ai-leadership/), allowing entrepreneurs and businesses to more easily adapt AI models to a variety of specialized uses, and are a vital part of a diverse and vibrant AI ecosystem. The target of this industry campaign was the [suggestions](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-accuses-chinas-moonshot-stealing-anthropics-fable-latest-ai-model-2026-06-30/) coming from some administration officials that they were about to impose export controls and other restrictions on Chinese open AI models in retaliation for alleged adversarial distillation from proprietary US models. But the campaign overshot its mark. Banning open AI models, whether foreign or domestic, is indeed a [terrible idea](https://www.justsecurity.org/150856/regulate-dont-ban-chinese-ai-models/), as the campaign urged, but it does not follow that they should be exempt from AI risk reduction requirements. Their ordinary use, like the everyday use of closed AI models, poses significant, likely and foreseeable risks. Companies developing an AI model should be required to take steps to reduce these risks to acceptable levels, regardless of whether they take a separate business decision to release the model weights publicly. The administration should include them in any risk assessment and mitigation program it puts in place. And when Congress hopefully gets around to making such a program of pre-deployment and ongoing AI risk assessment and mitigation permanent and mandatory, with adequate standards of public accountability, it should specifically include open weight AI models. This exclusion would seem to include the highly-capable Chinese open models that are [widely used](https://openrouter.ai/rankings#leaderboard-table) by US startups and enterprises, but also the American open models such as those offered by [Meta](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/meta-muse-glimmer-open-weight-ai.html) and start-ups like [Reflection AI](https://reflection.ai/news). Infra & Chips.content: * [Home](/) * [Tech](/personaltech) * [Artificial Intelligence](/artificial-intelligence) # Anthropic in Talks to Acquire Decart for $6B, Targeting 77% Gross Margins Before IPO #### Deal would bring 8x inference throughput gains to Claude’s costs before October Nasdaq listing By [William Chan](https://www.techtimes.com/reporters/william-chan) [Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324234/20260813/anthropic-talks-acquire-decart-6b-targeting-77-gross-margins-before-ipo.htm) [Share on Twitter](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Anthropic+in+Talks+to+Acquire+Decart+for+%246B%2C+Targeting+77%25+Gross+Margins+Before+IPO+https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324234/20260813/anthropic-talks-acquire-decart-6b-targeting-77-gross-margins-before-ipo.htm) [Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.techtimes.com%2Farticles%2F324234%2F20260813%2Fanthropic-talks-acquire-decart-6b-targeting-77-gross-margins-before-ipo.htm&title=Anthropic+in+Talks+to+Acquire+Decart+for+%246B%2C+Targeting+77%25+Gross+Margins+Before+IPO) [Share on Reddit](http://reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324234/20260813/anthropic-talks-acquire-decart-6b-targeting-77-gross-margins-before-ipo.htm&title=Anthropic+in+Talks+to+Acquire+Decart+for+%246B%2C+Targeting+77%25+Gross+Margins+Before+IPO) [Share on Flipboard](https://flipboard.com) [Share on Pocket](https://getpocket.com/edit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324234/20260813/anthropic-talks-acquire-decart-6b-targeting-77-gross-margins-before-ipo.htm) Anthropic is in advanced talks to acquire Israeli AI infrastructure startup Decart AI for approximately $6 billion — a deal that would be the Claude maker's largest known acquisition and would arrive as the company attempts to show public investors that its path to software-like profit margins is grounded in engineering, not just forecasts. Bloomberg [first reported the deal](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-said-talks-buy-startup-015017011.html) late Wednesday night; Reuters [separately confirmed the talks](https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/innov-nation/artc-anthropic-in-negotiations-to-acquire-israeli-decart-ai-for-6-billion-report) within hours. Both outlets reported that no agreement has been finalized and that discussions could still fall apart.
